title: A 96fsrms-Jitter, -70.6dBc-Fractional-Spur Cascaded PLL Employing Two MMDs with Shared DSM for Quantization Noise Cancellation
problem: Fractional-N PLLs suffer from quantization noise (Q-noise) and fractional spurs from the delta-sigma modulator (DSM). Existing quantization-error cancellation (QEC) approaches require intensive calibration with long settling times; multi-PLL architectures introduce mixing spurs requiring bulky analog filters; cascaded integer-fractional approaches leave fractional spurs in-band at near-integer channels.
motivation: Wireless transceivers and FMCW radar demand high-performance frequency synthesizers with fast settling time, low jitter, and minimal fractional spurs for reliable communication and sensing.
method: A cascaded PLL architecture employs two multi-modulus dividers (MMDs) sharing a single DSM for quantization noise cancellation. By operating the shared DSM at elevated frequency, Q-noise is pushed out of bandwidth and filtered naturally, while the dual-MMD structure suppresses fractional spurs in-band through noise subtraction without requiring intensive digital calibration.
key_novelty: Shared DSM dual-MMD cascaded PLL achieving calibration-free quantization noise cancellation with natural fractional-spur suppression via noise subtraction.
contributions: Calibration-free QEC architecture eliminating convergence-time bottleneck
Dual-MMD shared DSM design improving area/power vs. multi-PLL approaches
Fast settling time without sacrificing spectral purity for wireless/radar systems
baselines: Conventional QEC-based PLLs (requires calibration, longer settling)
Multi-PLL approaches (mixing spurs, bulky analog filter)
limitations: Not discussed; phase margin stability, temperature/PVT robustness, and power consumption not fully characterized.
primary_theme: Shared-DSM cascaded PLL for fractional-spur suppression
